To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel peak-pilated deep network (PPDNet) that uses a peak sample to supervise the feature responses of a non-peak sample, and the PPDNet is able to achieve the in- variance to expression intensities by implicitly learning the expression evolving process from a non-peak expression to a peak expression.

1) PPDN achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Cohn-Kanade and JAFFE databases; 2) The PPDN can be used as a plug-in to existing networks, such as AlexNet and VGGNet, to achieve state-of-the-art results; and 3) The PPDNs are robust against expression intensities.
the proposed PPDN achieves state-of-the-art performance on two public databases, namely CK+ and Oulu-CASIA.

a new approach for facial expression recognition, which can be applied to a large variety of applications.
a novel PPDN architecture that uses a peak-piloted training strategy for the facial expression recognition task.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a PPDN that is able to capture the expression evolution process from non-peak to peak expressions and thus can be used for the facial expression recognition task.

we propose a novel peak-pilated deep network that can effectively handle the problem of expression intensities and can be applied to other tasks that need to deal with the problem of expression variations.
we propose to use peak-piloted samples to supervise the training of deep network for the recognition of facial expressions.

the PPDN can achieve the invariances of expression intensity, head pose, and illumination.
a sample from a different subject with peak expression of the same type can be used to supervise the intermediate response of a sample of nonpeak expression from another subject.
a sample with peak facial expression is a good proxy to supervise a sample with nonpeak expression.
